title: Predicting Future Earnings Changes Using Machine Learning and Detailed Financial Data

scopes.description: The supplied R workflow embedded in CCDL Code 20220212.pdf: SEC XBRL tag and point-in-time preparation, Compustat OP and DuPont preparation, finalMatrix construction, and the supplied SGB/RF prediction and return evaluation branch. The source is a PDF container rather than a standalone driver; its input schemas and cross-stage handoffs remain incomplete.

requirements.description: Public SEC Financial Statement Data Sets are the matching source family for the code's SUB, NUM and TAG reads. The author datasheet uses filings from 2012 Q2 through 2018 Q1; code filters fiscal and GAAP consolidated filings and consumes submission, number and tag fields. The current SEC archive is publicly listed for the sample years, but its December 2024 historical reprocessing can change contents relative to the author's vintage.

routes.description: The official quarterly archives cover the author period and the official specification names matching SUB, NUM and TAG tables. Acquire the applicable quarterly ZIPs, extract/stage files for the authored /XBRL/sub, /XBRL/num and /XBRL/tag layout with the 2012–2018 directories used by the code, and preserve the current release version. Public access is verified; no data were downloaded. Reprocessed historical contents should be compared with the author's version as a fidelity check.
routes.expected_period: Author datasheet: SEC submissions 2012 Q2–2018 Q1; code reads yearly files for 2012–2018 and filters period values from 20120615 onward.

requirements.description: The supplied OP block reads the absent author-prepared compustat_op.csv using GVKEY and fyear panel keys, creates OP predictors with annual lags, and writes op_var.csv with cik and fyear. The final matrix later expects a cik/period join, so source fields, CIK mapping, fiscal-year mapping and lag history need the author's export contract.

routes.description: COMP.FUNDA is a catalogued annual fundamentals candidate with GVKEY and FYEAR metadata, but the required OP input fields, CIK relation, fyear-to-period conversion, update vintage and prior-year history are not verified. Catalog presence is not a successful data probe.
S&P/Compustat is a vendor product path, not a public download route. Entitlement, exact author fields, identifier/date mapping and annual lag history are unverified; no access barrier is inferred.

requirements.description: The supplied DuPont block reads the absent author-prepared compustat_np.csv, indexes it by LPERMNO and fyear, uses lag and lead values, and writes np_var.csv with cik and fyear. Required raw fields, CIK/security links, annual timing and the final cik/period mapping are unspecified.

routes.description: COMP.FUNDA and the CRSP/Compustat link table are catalogued candidates for a raw-source construction path, but the required DuPont fields, LPERMNO/CIK linkage, fyear-to-period mapping, vintages and lead/lag history are not established. This is not a confirmed replacement for compustat_np.csv.

Vendor Compustat data plus a compatible security-link source may provide a raw construction route, but no entitlement, field mapping, linkage history or matched export has been verified. No access barrier is inferred.

requirements.description: The matrix block reads the absent ibes_pro_forma.csv and merges it by TICKER and SEC period; later it retains inc_eps for classification. The author describes drift-adjusted pro forma earnings, but the export's fields, adjustment construction, filing/as-of date and ticker crosswalk are not supplied.

routes.description: ACTU_XEPSUS appears in the frozen catalog as an unadjusted non-EPS US actuals candidate. It is only a candidate: compatibility with author pro forma EPS, drift adjustment, TICKER/period, and inc_eps is not established.

The vendor page directs users to LSEG for data and pricing. It does not establish public access or identify the author's pro forma actuals measure, drift adjustment, period/as-of convention or export fields; entitlement remains unknown.

requirements.description: The matrix block reads the absent af.csv, computes forecast_period as SEC period plus twelve months and merges by TICKER and forecast_period; finalMatrix retains a field named af. The forecast definition, as-of date and export fields are not supplied.

routes.description: STATSUMU_XEPSUS appears in the frozen catalog as an unadjusted summary candidate with ticker, forecast-period and measure fields. The exact forecast measure, author af field, as-of history and merge contract remain unverified; catalog presence is not a successful probe.
The I/B/E/S vendor path is not a public dataset route. The exact forecast measure, as-of history, ticker linkage and file export remain unspecified; no access barrier is inferred.

requirements.description: The matrix reads the absent crsp.csv and merges by cik and period; later code consumes sar as the size-adjusted return field. The CRSP return construction, CIK/security link, formation timing, size adjustment and any transaction-cost treatment are not defined by this export contract.

routes.description: Monthly stock and CCM link-table catalog candidates could support a raw-source construction, but no successful bounded read, CIK/period linkage, share/return treatment, size-adjustment or author sar export mapping is established.
CRSP stock data are a vendor route, not a public dataset route. Entitlement, CIK mapping, required history and size-adjusted SAR construction remain unverified; no access barrier is inferred.

issues.description: The substantive R program is embedded in a 16-page PDF rather than supplied as a standalone driver. Static visual review supports working-copy extraction, comment restoration for visually wrapped comment continuations, and reflow of the visible expression/regex wraps on pages 8, 11, 14 and 15; it does not support changing formulas, estimator settings or unknown input contracts.

The code consumes compustat_op.csv, compustat_np.csv, ibes_pro_forma.csv, af.csv and crsp.csv, but the release contains no producers or complete field/date/identifier contracts for these prepared inputs. Frozen catalog candidates are discovery only; author-prepared inputs and compatible raw construction are both unverified.

The model block requires finalMatrix.csv and reads SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID, but the task range and accession-string split contract are not supplied. The final comparison also merges an object named compare with no producer in the supplied PDF. A local wrapper could set the task variable, but its values and the comparison-model handoff remain unknown.

The visible matrix starts with six base fields and the tag loop only assigns when the constructed tag name already exists, so the shown block does not create those dynamic tag columns. Separately, common_standard_tags.csv is written headerless with one tag vector, while its consumer refers to tax$tag and tax$datatype. The intended tag-column and datatype producer contract needs clarification.

The OP and NP producers export cik and fyear, but finalMatrix joins each export by cik and period. The source does not define a fyear-to-period representation or confirm why output keys and join keys differ. Do not invent a year-to-date mapping.

mtrx is visibly initialized without TICKER, yet joins use TICKER. The block also requires Assets_0 and Assets_1 and retains inc_eps, af and sar, whose producer/column contracts are not fully shown. Request export headers and the CIK-to-TICKER, period and dependent-variable definitions; do not invent an earnings proxy or return definition.

The bootstrap block initializes bootstrap with bootstrap_55_sar and bootstrap_64_sar, writes into random_dist, then reads mean_bootstrap_55_sar/64_sar and final$hedge_55_sar/64_sar fields not created in the visible code. Clarify the intended object names, aggregation producer and hedge-field producer without changing the 10,000-iteration analysis.

The model formula subtracts op_var and np_var by name, while the matrix code uses objects with those names as character vectors of predictor columns. The intended formula exclusion semantics and surviving feature set are not specified; preserve the authored formula pending clarification.

evidence.description: Datasheet sample is described as SEC submissions from 2012 Q2 through 2018 Q1, with a June 15, 2012 reporting-period cutoff.
evidence.quote:
1) We obtained submission and numerical data from XBRL filings submitted between the
   second quarter of 2012 and the first quarter of 2018. We retained only the observations with a
   non-missing reporting period ending on or after June 15, 2012.

evidence.description: Datasheet names pro forma I/B/E/S earnings, Compustat predictors, I/B/E/S analyst forecasts and CRSP stock price data.
evidence.quote:
3) We obtained pro forma earnings from I/B/E/S and kept only the pro forma earnings that
   differ from the U.S GAAP earnings. We adjusted the pro forma earnings for a firm-specific
   trend by subtracting the average change in earnings over the past four years. We merged the
   pro forma earnings data with the data from Step (2).
4) We merged the data from Step 3) with a) firm-level financial data from Compustat for the
   construction of predictors in Ou and Penman (1989) and Nissim and Penman (2001), b)
   analyst forecasts from I/B/E/S, and c) stock price data from CRSP. We excluded observations
   without a stock price at the portfolio formation date.

evidence.description: Datasheet describes current and lagged fiscal-year values, asset scaling, annual percentage changes and zero replacement.
evidence.quote:
8) For each firm-year observation from Step 7), we selected numerical data that correspond to
   current and lagged values by using the reporting period to identify current and lagged fiscal
   years. We divided each monetary item by its respective fiscal year’s total assets. For each
   numerical item, we created an annual percentage change variable. We retained only the
   current variable, lagged variable, and percentage changes.
9) The missing predictor values are all replaced with zeros.
